subject: chemistry
title: Molecules: Atoms Bonded
welcome_lead: Two or more atoms holding hands chemically: you've just met a molecule.
meta_desc: Discover molecules in this KS3 chemistry adventure on atoms bonded together.
final_note: You now know the difference between an atom and a molecule.

concepts.def: Two or more atoms chemically bonded together.
Force holding atoms together in a molecule.
Molecule of just two atoms, like O₂.
Molecule of three atoms, like H₂O or CO₂.
Same atoms bonded together (e.g. H₂, O₂).

walkthroughs.body_html:
A molecule is two or more atoms chemically bonded together. The atoms may be the same or different.

2+ atoms = molecule.

O₂ — two oxygen atoms (the air you breathe).
H₂O — two hydrogen + one oxygen (water).
CO₂ — one carbon + two oxygen (the gas you breathe out).

N₂, H₂, Cl₂ are also diatomic.

If the atoms in the molecule are the same element (like O₂), it's still an element.

If the atoms are different elements (like H₂O), it's a compound.
